title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 3 — Angles Recap
question: Can you name angles and find missing angles on a line, around a point, in a triangle and on parallel lines?
intro: **Quick recap:** straight line \(180^\circ\); around a point \(360^\circ\); triangle \(180^\circ\); opposite, corresponding (F) and alternate (Z) angles are equal; co-interior (C) angles add up to \(180^\circ\).

questions.title: 3.1 · Name the angle
questions.prompt: An angle measures \(135^\circ\). What type of angle is it?

questions.title: 3.1 · Reflex angle
questions.solution:
\[\boxed{250^\circ} \to \text{reflex}\]

\(180^\circ\) is a straight angle, and \(175^\circ\) is obtuse.

questions.title: 3.2 · Straight line
questions.prompt: Two angles on a straight line are \(118^\circ\) and \(x\). Find \(x\). Give the answer in degrees.
questions.solution:
\[x = 180^\circ - 118^\circ = \boxed{62^\circ}\]

\(242\) uses \(360^\circ\), which is for angles around a point.

questions.title: 3.2 · Three angles on a line
questions.prompt: Three angles on a straight line are \(45^\circ\), \(70^\circ\) and \(x\). Find \(x\). Give the answer in degrees.

questions.title: 3.3 · Around a point
questions.prompt: Angles around a point are \(140^\circ\), \(95^\circ\) and \(x\). Find \(x\). Give the answer in degrees.
questions.solution:
\(140^\circ + 95^\circ = 235^\circ\):

\[x = 360^\circ - 235^\circ = \boxed{125^\circ}\]

Using \(180^\circ\) gives a negative angle — a sign the wrong total was used.

questions.title: 3.3 · Crossing lines
questions.prompt: Two straight lines cross. One angle is \(58^\circ\). Find the angle **next to** it. Give the answer in degrees.
questions.solution:
Neighbouring angles sit on a straight line:

\[180^\circ - 58^\circ = \boxed{122^\circ}\]

\(58^\circ\) is the **opposite** angle, not the neighbour.

questions.title: 3.3 · Four angles around a point
questions.prompt: Angles around a point are \(75^\circ\), \(105^\circ\), \(90^\circ\) and \(x\). Find \(x\). Give the answer in degrees.

questions.title: 3.4 · Triangle
questions.prompt: A triangle has angles of \(48^\circ\) and \(67^\circ\). Find the third angle. Give the answer in degrees.
questions.solution:
\(48^\circ + 67^\circ = 115^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 115^\circ = \boxed{65^\circ}\]

\(245\) uses \(360^\circ\) — a triangle's angles add up to \(180^\circ\).

questions.title: 3.4 · Isosceles triangle
questions.prompt: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of \(30^\circ\). Find **one** of its two equal base angles. Give the answer in degrees.
questions.solution:
\[(180^\circ - 30^\circ)\div2 = 150^\circ\div2 = \boxed{75^\circ}\]

\(150\) forgets to share between the two base angles.

questions.title: 3.4 · Exterior angle
questions.prompt: The two inside angles opposite an exterior angle are \(55^\circ\) and \(62^\circ\). Find the exterior angle. Give the answer in degrees.
questions.solution:
\[55^\circ + 62^\circ = \boxed{117^\circ}\]

\(63\) is the third **inside** angle (\(180^\circ - 117^\circ\)), next to the exterior angle on the straight line.

questions.title: 3.5 · Co-interior angles
questions.prompt: Two co-interior angles lie between parallel lines. One is \(108^\circ\). Find the other. Give the answer in degrees.
questions.solution:
\[180^\circ - 108^\circ = \boxed{72^\circ}\]

\(108\) would be right for corresponding or alternate angles, which are equal.

questions.title: 3.5 · Alternate angles
questions.prompt: Alternate angles (a **Z** shape) on parallel lines …
questions.solution:
\[\boxed{\text{equal}}\]

Adding up to \(180^\circ\) is the rule for co-interior angles (a **C** shape).

takeaway: Line 180°, point 360°, triangle 180°; opposite, corresponding and alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles add up to 180°; an exterior angle equals the two opposite inside angles.
